action_summary: A refactoring sentence names a SYMBOL, and the compiler could only read paths. Measured on 34648e4f: 'Rename the function add to plus in the python module <root>/pkg/calc.py and save the report to <root>/ren.json.' scored python.refactor.rename_symbol.v1 at 22 -- the highest prose score of any candidate -- and was then dropped with GOAL_INPUT_BINDING_REQUIRED module. The same sentence reached document.convert.markdown_pdf.pandoc_weasyprint at score 4, which bound markdown_path to the .py file the sentence named and reported PASS for work nobody asked for. The three rename capabilities were present, correct, and UNBINDABLE FROM LANGUAGE: _bind_inputs produced text, goal, url, *_path, *_argv, *_root and *_dir values and nothing else, so module, qualname, old_symbol, new_symbol, old_param and new_param were unreachable in every registered capability that declares them; python_executable and timeout_s -- 23 of the 46 unreachable rows -- were unreachable a second way, because the binder raised on a knob the adapter already defaults. SIX fixes, no new capability, no model: (1) an identifier grammar reads the symbol, its scope and the module the sentence names, and can only ever read what the sentence spells; (2) module and source_root are decided as ONE binding, because the adapter resolves module relative to the root; (3) an execution knob is defaulted when the sentence is silent and bound when it states a number; (4) a template slot the sentence legitimately leaves unsaid is omitted instead of raising, so a bound-and-selected capability no longer dies at dispatch; (5) run_tests -- the slot that makes a refactor's verification law checkable -- binds, and falls back to the test module that already sits beside the stated module relative to source_root, because the adapter's own law says a blind edit is not a rename; (6) the front binder pins those slots to the sentence-reading binder instead of a generic type binder that has no grammar for an identifier.

load_bearing_primary.interpretation: A capability is chosen by what the sentence's verb acts ON, not by which verbs the sentence contains, and a sentence that names a route has chosen it. 'write the repair REPORT' and 'write the FIX' are the same verb in different frames, and only the second is a request to overwrite the input; VerbNet's frames and FrameNet's frame elements are the established statement of that distinction, and the machine already had both capabilities, so nothing had to be built -- only the sentence had to be read the same way by all five readers.

obs_blocker.delete_bypass_substitute_options: Teaching the front compiler a rename-shaped special case was rejected: it would generalise to exactly one verb and leave extract_function, the renamer's sibling and every future symbol-taking capability unreachable. Requiring the caller to spell the capability id was rejected as making the system's best verbs unusable from language. Inferring the module from the only .py file on disk was rejected: the sentence names it, so the binder reads it. Relaxing gate PASS to accept PASS_BLIND was rejected: it would delete the verification law to make a blind run look credited; the referee suite is discovered beside the module instead.
obs_blocker.intrinsic_or_path_specific: Path-specific to five readers of the same sentence: the ranker's effect tokens, the admission's command-slot test, the promise reader's verb match and report shape, and the measurement's own goal text.
obs_blocker.surviving_causal_blocker: No refactoring capability was missing: three rename verbs and the extract-function verb were registered and verified. What was missing was the vocabulary to BIND them -- the same gap the project has hit in every other family, where a capability exists and the compiler cannot say what it needs. The fix reuses the existing binder and the existing sentence tokenizer; nothing new is registered.
